findings.title: G4 at notice level refuses every block of a notice over one contradiction, including blocks whose own title confirms their number. The cost is about 5x what the decision states, and a free variant keeps every catch
findings.evidence: Re-ran g3_port.py into scratchpad/u8/critic-measure.json; it is byte-identical to measurement-u7.json (FINAL 11/13, 53/61, FR 4/1,762). Replayed variants with scratchpad/u8/critic/variants.py and g4block.py on the in-sample set and on the OOS 50 (u8-oos o1/o2 skeptic-final labels). (a) The notice level buys almost nothing. Block-level G4 alone catches 51/61 other-wrong and 11/13 multi with 0 false refusals in-sample, and 100/100 with 3 false refusals OOS. Making it notice-level adds only 5267810 RES-7 ('Pakiet 1A') and RES-8 ('Pakiet'). It costs 4 right blocks in-sample (5051007 RES-1..3 'Pakiet nr 1/2/3', 5267810 RES-1 'PAKIET 1') and 19 OOS (8286472 RES-1..8 'zadanie k', 5416534 RES-1..14 'Pakiet k'). Every one of the 23 refused blocks has a title naming exactly its own printed number. (b) The cost is understated. The decision says 4 FR (0.23%, at most 0.58%) and about 4 k coincidental rights corpus-wide (lines 112, 249, 336). OOS gives 22 right blocks refused in 50 Tenders (22/319 = 6.9% of right blocks). Pooled, 26 per 200 Tenders × 156,123 ≈ 20 k. The block-level Clopper–Pearson treats clustered blocks as independent. The real unit is the notice: 55 notices carry any designator-bearing matched block, 48 of them all-right, so the 95% CP upper bound is about 7.4% of such notices. Each holds about 12 blocks on average, and some hold 139 (5284511), 67 (5259203) or 48 (5106209). (c) The carve-out protecting 5218711 works by accident. CAN 18184190 prints 5/6/7 on 'Lot 3.B/3.C/3.D' (designator 3). Its blocks are spared only because N = {1,2,3,4}. A CN with 7 or more lots would make those 16 blocks match and contradict, and the notice level would refuse the 20 right 'Lot k' blocks with them. (d) Variant 'title-confirm': in a G4-fired notice, keep a block whose own Dn heads are exactly {p}. Results are identical: in-sample 53/61 + 11/13, OOS 100/100. False refusals drop to 0/1,762 in-sample and 3/319 OOS; the 3 are the G3 lexicon FP '(pakiet N pozycji)'. A threshold of 2 or more contradicting blocks before the notice level fires also changes nothing measured: every G4 notice has 2 to 29 contradicting blocks.
findings.fix: Change the rule: (1) G4 is block-level always. (2) The notice-level extension fires only when 2 or more matched blocks of the notice contradict. (3) Inside a fired notice, a block whose own title designators' heads are exactly {p} keeps its lot. This never keys by title, so step 9 stands. Update the 5051007 test to keep RES-1..3 on LOT-1..3. Re-state the cost line (about 4 k → about 0) and the port-parity numbers (FINAL 11/13, 53/61, FR 0).

findings.title: The designator grammar has concrete false-positive paths, one in the decision's own control Tender's CN and two seen OOS. Free fixes exist
findings.evidence: Probed lot_designators.designators() (scratchpad/u8/critic/lex.py, scan.py, lexvar.py). (1) The spaced-dash range rule. 4667265's own CN 12540916 prints TED-LOT_TITLE 'Część 1 – 50 miejsc', which the reader expands to lots 1..50, and 'Część 2 - 80 miejsc', expanded to 2..80. The SELFTEST control passes only because CAN 16915317 reformatted them as 'Część 1 50 - miejsc.' and 'Część 2- 80 miejsc.'. An award that copies its lot title, the common case, gives Dn = {1,2} and G3 refuses both right blocks. Other probes: 'Lot 1 - 5 ordinateurs portables' gives 1..5, 'Lot 12 – 15 sites' gives 12..15, 'Lot 3 - 2 véhicules' gives [3,2]. (2) Compounds and position words. 'Pakiet 8 poz. 6 i 7' and 'Pakiet 8 poz. 6-7' give [8,6,7]; 'Pakiet 3 (poz. 1-12)' gives [3,1..12]. When the compound fails, `poz` restarts as a lot keyword. OOS o1 8286472 shows '(pakiet 8 pozycji) … - zadanie 4' read as [8,4], so G3 hits 3 right blocks, masked only by G4. The OOS o2 counterfactual shows 'Pakiet 16 zad.1' trips G3 on 22 blocks, because zad. is not a compound half. (3) The Spanish article. 'Mantenimiento de los 4 ascensores del lote 2' gives [4,2] (G3), and 'limpieza de los 3 edificios' gives [3] (a G4 contradiction that refuses the whole notice). Lowercase `los` is matched because KW_RE is IGNORECASE. None of the 4,035 distinct cached title texts has lowercase 'los <n>', so the samples have no Spanish exposure to measure. Fixes measured in lexvar.py: tight dash only (a spaced dash ends the list), and `Los/Lose/LOS` case-sensitive (German nouns are capitalised). Each keeps SELFTEST 35/35 and gives identical catches and FR in-sample (53/61, 11/13, 4) and OOS (100/100, 22). Across the 4,035 cached titles the tight-dash change alters exactly the two 4667265 CN titles. Do NOT drop `pozycja` outright: about 100 cached lot titles are 'Pozycja nr k' used as the lot designator.
findings.fix: Change the rule (reader) and add the cases to SELFTEST: (a) DASH = tight dash only, with 'Część 1 – 50 miejsc' → [1] and 'Lot 1 - 5 ordinateurs' → [1] as cases. (b) Match `Los/Lose` case-sensitively. (c) A compound's second half accepts a list or range and `zad./zadanie`, and stays ONE head. A position word (`poz/pozycja/pozice/položka`) is a lot keyword only when no lot/pakiet/część clause precedes it in the same title. `pakiet N pozycji/pozycje` (a count) is not a designator. Re-run the port and the OOS 50 before the build's parity bar is frozen.

findings.title: The new read-back bar's P = 0.95 ignores its own 'any new shape reopens' clause, which pushes the real pass probability back to about 0.5–0.65. 'Guarded shape' has no operational definition
findings.evidence: The arithmetic is right. At p = 5/180 = 0.0278: P(0 of 30) = 0.430 and P(≤2 of 30) = 0.950. At the CP upper bound 0.0636: 0.139 and 0.702. The old 30/30 bar on the deployed rule (6.7%) passed with only 0.126, so the original bar was miscalibrated, and recomputing it before the next draw is principled in form. Pooling the OOS 50 (0/50 residual) gives 5/230 = 2.2%, with P(≤2) = 0.973, so the in-sample residual estimate holds up. But the bar's third clause reopens on any wrong block of a shape not in the five-row table. The 5 residual Tenders are 5 distinct shapes, all singletons, so a fresh residual Tender is most likely a new shape. Let q be the chance that a residual Tender shows a new shape. With q = 1 / 0.75 / 0.5, P(pass) ≈ 0.43 / 0.53 / 0.65 at 2.8%, and 0.52 / 0.61 / 0.72 at 2.2%. That is the same failure mode (failing a correct build more often than not) that the decision uses to reject 30/30. Also, 'guarded shape' versus 'residual shape' is a judgement call. A counter CAN whose titles carry no designator could be read as G4's shape or as 4968281's. The decision's (e) also does not say to exclude the OOS 50 (u8-oos/draw.json requires it) or the s150/f30/m77.
findings.fix: Change the bar to operational, pre-computed criteria. (i) Parity: on every block of the fresh 30, the served lot equals the g3_port replay lot (0 divergences, deterministic). (ii) At most 2 of 30 Tenders carry a judged-wrong block that the port also keeps, of any shape (P ≈ 0.95–0.97). (iii) A new residual shape is recorded and filed, not a reopen. Reopen only on a parity break or 3 or more of 30. State P(pass) for the bar as written, and exclude the OOS 50, s150, f30 and m77 from the draw.

findings.title: G3 counts distinct designators, not distinct lots, so two positions of one pakiet read as a multi-lot award
findings.evidence: Rule step 3: 'Dn holds two or more distinct designators', where a compound (head, position) is ONE designator. designators('Pakiet 8 poz. 6, Pakiet 8 poz. 7') gives [('8','6'),('8','7')]. Both heads are 8, but they are two distinct tuples, so G3 refuses a right block printed 8. 'Pakiet N poz. M' is a live Polish pattern (4945774 × 45, 5267810 × 32 in the samples). Counting distinct heads instead (variant g3heads in scratchpad/u8/critic/variants.py) gives identical catches and FR in-sample (53/61, 11/13, FR 4) and OOS (100/100, FR 22).
findings.fix: Change the rule: G3 fires when the heads of Dn hold 2 or more distinct values. Add 'Pakiet 8 poz. 6, Pakiet 8 poz. 7' printed 8 as a keep case in the tests.

findings.title: Further lexicon risks are unpinned, and notice-level G4 turns any one of them into a whole-notice refusal
findings.evidence: Reader outputs (scratchpad/u8/critic/lex.py). Romance 'a' is read as a list conjunction, not a range: 'Lotes 1 a 5' gives [1,5]. A multi-lot block printed 3 with that title is then a G4 contradiction that refuses the whole notice, not just a G3 refusal of the one block. Other outputs: 'Lotti da 1 a 5' gives [] (recall). 'Lot 2, 3 ans' gives [2,3]. 'Pakiet 5, 2 szt.' gives [5,2]. 'Szkolenie dla grupy 20 osób' (training for a group of 20) gives [20]. 'Spare parts 2 years' gives [2]. 'Realizacja zadania 2 programu, część 3' gives [2,3]. 'Lot 2 (remplace le lot 5 infructueux)' gives [2,5]. Upper-case single-letter Roman: 'LOT C' gives 100 and 'LOT MIX' gives 1009; the N filter catches most of these, but V, X and I land inside N. Risk 1's '0 of 1,762' is in-sample: the grammar was tuned on these titles (the '2- 80' spacing rule exists for 4667265). The OOS 50 already surfaced two new FP shapes in two Tenders (see the grammar finding).
findings.fix: Keep the guards, but add these strings to SELFTEST as negative cases (expected output written down, fixed or explicitly accepted). Adopting the G4 title-confirm and ≥2-contradiction change bounds the blast radius of any single FP. Rewrite Risk 1 to say the false-refusal rate is in-sample, and cite the OOS result (3/319 G3 FPs) alongside it.

findings.title: Multilingual titles: G3/G4 take the union across languages, G5 accepts one agreeing language. This is inconsistent and unmeasured
findings.evidence: The rule reads 'every value, every language and every ordinal' into one designator set, so one mistranslated language can create a G3 multi or a G4 contradiction (notice-wide). G5 deliberately treats one language agreeing with the matched lot as agreement (8303947). Parsed values carry `lang` (for example 17500557 RES-1: EN/DA/DE ordinals 0/1/2), so per-language evaluation is implementable. Evidence base: only 62 of 2,256 matched blocks (in-sample + OOS) carry more than one title value, and 1 has differing designator sets across values (5004315 RES-2, ordinals naming 2.1/2.2/2.3). The union rule is effectively untested on translated titles.
findings.fix: Change the rule. Compute Dn per language, taking the union over ordinals within one language. A block does not contradict (G4) if any language's Dn contains p or agrees with l's text. G3 fires only if some single language's Dn has 2 or more heads. Add a translated-title test (for example a 23-language block where one language has a typo).

findings.title: The text-field spec differs between the decision prose, the port and the fold's facts, so the port-parity bar may fail for reasons unrelated to the guards
findings.evidence: Lot side. The decision lists TED-LOT_TITLE, r209 TED-TITLE, TED-LOT_DESCRIPTION and TED-SHORT_DESCR. g3_port LOT_TEXT_FIELDS adds TED-SHORT_CONTRACT_DESCRIPTION. The build reads LotState facts, and the fold's TEXTS table (crates/ingest/src/project.rs:240-276) also maps TED-SHORT_DESCRIPTION_CONTRACT, plus TED-TITLE_CONTRACT and TED-CONTRACT_TITLE when lot-scoped, to title and description. Facts are superseded per field across versions, while the port keeps only the latest lot section's texts. Block side. The in-progress build decodes titles through served_text (publisher escapes); the port reads raw values. Scope. On CANs without their own lot sections (the only ones the guards read), the cache holds TED-CONTRACT_TITLE (2,269 values) and TED-TITLE_CONTRACT (110). TED-TITLE (18) appears only on CANs with their own lot sections, so it is dead in scope and untested. Any of these differences can move G4's agreement set (Dlot) or G5's keys, so 'FINAL 11/13, 53/61, 4' parity can fail with no guard bug.
findings.fix: Change the spec. Define the lot side as 'the lot's title/description facts as folded at the award version' and the block side as 'decoded with served_text'. Make g3_port read the same field table (the TEXTS list) and the same decode, then regenerate measurement-u7.json before using it as the parity bar. Note that TED-TITLE is out of scope for R2.0.8 awards.

findings.title: The combined drain with 570 creates newly matched blocks (G2 narrowed) that no sample covers, and the fresh-30 population cannot draw them
findings.evidence: The replay of s150, f30 and m77 has 0 G2 refusals (scratchpad/u8/critic/why.py). The 2594 corrected population excludes G2-refused Tenders by construction. 570 computes G2 on the remapped carry, so in the combined refold some of those Tenders' R2.0.8 blocks become matchable for the first time, and G3–G6 run on them unmeasured. 570 measured 0 R2.0.8 awards after a remapped notice, but only on 22 R2.0.8 CANs (95% CP upper bound ≈ 15%). Read-back (e) draws from readback/population.json (the 2594 corrected set), so it cannot sample them. The drain scope itself is fine: every guardable block has a TED-LOT_NO or TED-LOT_NUMBER on its CAN.
findings.fix: Change the bar: draw the fresh 30 from the combined wet run's corrected set, or add a stratum of Tenders whose award blocks go from null to a lot only in the combined drain. Have (f) attribute these blocks separately from 568-u7 reverts and 570 remaps.

findings.title: Building the guards rather than rolling back is defensible (keep). The residual accounting overstates the harm 568 adds and does not reach consumers
findings.evidence: After the guards, the uniform in-sample blocks are 1,102 right against 10 wrong (0.85%), and the OOS 50 are 297 right against 0 wrong. Pooled, 5 of 230 Tenders (2.2%) carry a wrong block. Of the 10 wrong blocks: 4861483 × 4 was already on the wrong Tender before 568 (a weld, issue 364). 5364153 RES-4's title equals LOT-3's title once its '3a' prefix is stripped (the parent lot). 5267907 × 2 sit on one of two textually identical placeholder lots ('Produits frais et surgelés'), so only winners move. The harm new with 568 is 3 blocks (4854639 RES-9/10, 4968281 RES-1) in 2 of 230 Tenders. Rolling back discards about 1,400 right placements in the same samples to avoid that. The /docs caveat (line 295) lists only what stays on the Tender. It does not tell consumers who read lot_results[].lot as fact that the lot comes from the award's printed number, nor that a known residual exists.
findings.fix: Keep (build the guards, do not roll back). Re-state the residual as 568-attributable versus inherited (364 weld, parent lot, identical placeholders). Extend the /docs caveat sentence: an R2.0.8 award's lot is inferred from its printed number against the contract notice's lots, with a recorded residual of about 2% of such Tenders.

findings.title: There is a cheap guard for the paraphrased CAN-only renumbering residual (4854639 RES-9/10). The containment test was rejected without the condition that removes its false refusals
findings.evidence: scratchpad/u8/critic/g5sub.py tests a stricter G5. The block's content tokens (len > 2, non-numeric, stopwords dropped) must be a subset of exactly one other numbered lot's title tokens, AND must share no content token with the matched lot's own title. It catches 4854639 RES-7/8/9/10 ('Snagging' and 'Painting' against LOT-5 '5. Snagging'; RES-9/10 belong to '6. Repair painting'). It has 0 false refusals on 1,762 in-sample and 319 OOS right blocks. Plain containment without the no-shared-token condition refuses 11 right blocks in this reconstruction, for example 4854639 RES-1..6 'Cranes' on '1. Service for Cranes…', 8367203 RES-6 and 8313642 RES-1. All 11 share tokens with their own lot. Caveat: it is fit on one Tender and has 0 OOS hits.
findings.fix: Optional change to the rule: add this as G5b, only if a fresh OOS draw confirms 0 false refusals. Otherwise keep the residual row, but correct its 'why not guarded' text: containment fails only without the no-shared-token-with-own-lot condition.

review_findings.title: The Rust designator reader is case-insensitive where lot_designators.py is case-sensitive, and it accepts lower-case Roman words as list tokens, so G3/G4 read titles differently from the measured reference
review_findings.evidence:
How I checked: I compiled project.rs lines 7950-8441 (plus crosswalk::fold_diacritics and fold_greek_tonos) into a standalone binary under the scratchpad (rev568u8/) and compared it with lot_designators.designators(). Nothing in the repo was touched.

Where it agrees: SELFTEST 35/35, the implementer's 9 edge cases 9/9, and all 44,000 single-line text values in u7-cache.jsonl.gz.

Where it diverges: 17 of 58,262 fuzz strings, plus targeted cases. There are two causes.

(1) Case of separators and range words. The reference compiles only KW_RE, POS_RE and POSTFIX_RE with re.IGNORECASE. NEXT_RE and FIRST_RE are case-sensitive, so the list conjunctions and range words only match in lower case. Rust's designator_next (spaced_word at 8222, using DESIGNATOR_CONJUNCTIONS 8002 and DESIGNATOR_RANGE_WORDS 8006) matches through designator_prefix, which case-folds. Examples (reference vs Rust):
- 'LOTS 3 ET 2': [3] vs [3,2]
- 'Lots 3 Et 2': [3] vs [3,2]
- 'CZĘŚĆ NR 1 I 2': [1] vs [1,2]
- 'ОБОСОБЕНИ ПОЗИЦИИ 5, 6 И 7': [5,6] vs [5,6,7]
- 'LOTES 1 Y 2': [1] vs [1,2]
- 'PAKIETY 1 DO 4' and 'LOTS 1 À 4': [1] vs 1..4

(2) Lower-case Roman list tokens. designator_number_at (8133) returns a lower-case Roman word as a list token ('in any case'). In the reference's lists, ROMAN is upper-case only, so the list never starts. Examples (reference vs Rust):
- 'Lot vi, VII': [] vs [7]
- 'lot i, X': [] vs [10]
- 'Lot c, D': [] vs [500]
- 'Lot mix, II': [] vs [2]
This also breaks the decision's own text ('an UPPER-CASE Roman numeral').

What it changes in the guards, on a Tender whose lots print 1-3:
- A block printing 2 titled 'LOTS 3 ET 2'. The reference gets Dn={3}, p=2 is not in it, so G4 fires and the whole notice stays on the Tender. Rust gets Dn={2,3}, so G4 does not fire; only G3 refuses that block, and the notice's other blocks keep their lots.
- A block printing 1 titled 'CZĘŚĆ NR 1 I 2'. The reference fires no guard (LOT-1). Rust refuses it by G3.

These shapes were not measured. The cache holds 41 all-caps keyword titles but none with an upper-case separator, so whole-cache parity holds without covering them. The header comment ('regex construct by construct') and the test's parity claim do not hold here.
review_findings.fix:
Choose one reading on purpose and pin it with tests.

Option A, reference parity:
- In designator_next, compare DESIGNATOR_CONJUNCTIONS and DESIGNATOR_RANGE_WORDS exactly, without designator_fold.
- In designator_number_at, return a Roman token only for an upper-case MDCLXVI word. The postfix scan can keep reading any case, because POSTFIX_RE is IGNORECASE and only norm_number drops lower case.

Option B, keep case-insensitive separators (the decision says 'Case-insensitive after NFC'):
- Add re.IGNORECASE for the separators in lot_designators.py's NEXT_RE.
- Re-run g3_port.py and confirm FINAL stays 11/13, 53/61, FR 4.
- Record the choice in decision-u7.md.

Fix (2) under either option.

In both cases, add 'LOTS 3 ET 2', 'CZĘŚĆ NR 1 I 2', 'PAKIETY 1 DO 4' and 'Lot vi, VII' to lot_designators_reads_lists_ranges_roman_and_compounds.

review_findings.title: The |N| < 2 exemption is not pinned by any test, and the one-lot test's docstring wrongly says the exemption is what keeps the block
review_findings.evidence: I removed the early return at project.rs:7746 (`if n.len() < 2 { return refused; }`), through an env-gated instrumented build. All 223 `project::` tests still passed, `the_text_guards_never_fire_on_a_one_lot_tender` included. That test only fails when the exemption AND the Dn filter are both removed (mutant `g3raw,nexempt`). The reason: with |N| = 1, Dn is a subset of N, so it holds at most one designator. G3 cannot fire, and G4 cannot contradict, because the matched block's printed p is that one head. So 4514627 RES-1 ('lots no1, 2, 5, …' on a one-lot CN) is kept by the Dn filter, not by the exemption, and the docstring at 21928 is false. The exemption changes outcomes only for G6, plus G5 when two lots print the same number. In the port's measurement-rerun.json, 0 matched blocks rely on the exemption alone, so no cached chain can pin it. I proved this with a temporary test, since removed: CN `r208_cn(1, &["1"])` plus a CAN block printing TED-LOT_NUMBER 1 and 2. On the build as delivered it gives [Some("LOT-1")]; under the mutant it gives [None]. For context, every other lens mutant was killed: G3 off, G4 off, G4 block-level, G4 without lot-text agreement, G4 reading unmatched blocks, G5 off, G5 without agreement, G5 all-languages agreement, G5 counting Tender titles, G6 off, re-keying refused blocks by title, the bucket path dropping award_text, reading Organization children's titles, and a compound read as two designators. All 35 SELFTEST cases are ported, and the chain data matches u7-cache.jsonl.gz for every named id.
review_findings.fix: Add an ADDED-shape case to `the_text_guards_never_fire_on_a_one_lot_tender`: a one-lot Tender (lot prints 1) and an award block printing two TED-LOT_NUMBERs (1, 2). It must keep LOT-1, and `g568_fold_without_guards` must agree. Correct the docstring: the Dn filter, not the exemption, keeps 4514627 RES-1. The exemption is what keeps a G6 block, or a duplicate-number G5 block, on a one-lot Tender.

review_findings.title: G4 running first (over blocks that G3/G6 would refuse) is not pinned
review_findings.evidence: The decision says G4 is notice-level and evaluated first. I added a mutant where G4's contradiction scan skips blocks that G3 or G6 refuse (G4 after G3/G6, over the remaining blocks only). All 223 `project::` tests passed. In the port's measurement-rerun.json, 0 of 269 notices differ between the two orders, so no cached chain can pin it. I proved this with a temporary test, since removed: CN printing 1-3; CAN RES-1 printed 1 and titled 'Lots 2 and 3' (G3, and it contradicts), RES-2 printed 2 with no title. The build as delivered gives [None, None]; the mutant gives [None, Some("LOT-2")].
review_findings.fix: Add an ADDED-shape test like the one above: a G3 block that also contradicts, next to an agreeing block, and assert the whole notice stays on the Tender. Alternatively, reduce 5020611's CAN to RES-3 (printed 3, names 5/10-13) plus an added block with no title.

review_findings.title: G5's "exactly one OTHER lot" condition is not pinned; the 4889588 control never reaches it
review_findings.evidence: I changed `.count() == 1` to `>= 1` (mutant `g5one`). All 223 `project::` tests passed. 4889588 ('Toksyna botulinowa' titles lots 3 and 9) is settled by the own-lot agreement check before the count runs: each block's title equals its own lot's title. The same is true in g3_port.py (`not (keys & mine)` comes first). I proved this with a temporary test, since removed: lots 1-3 titled Alpha, Beta and Beta, and a block printed 1 titled 'Beta'. The build as delivered keeps LOT-1; the mutant gives None.
review_findings.fix: Add an ADDED-shape case to `an_award_titled_as_another_lot_stays_on_the_tender_4854639`: a block whose title matches two OTHER lots' titles and not its own keeps its lot.

review_findings.title: G4's agreement through the matched lot's description is not pinned (only through its title)
review_findings.evidence: The decision says G4 agreement reads the designators of 'l's own title or description facts'. I made the lot side read only `title` (mutant `g4titleonly`). All 223 `project::` tests passed. The generator notes that no reduced chain needed lot descriptions, and 5071935 agrees only through LOT-3's TED-LOT_TITLE. I proved this with a temporary test, since removed: CN 1-3 where LOT-1's TED-LOT_DESCRIPTION is 'Lot 3 of the old plan', and a block printed 1 titled 'Lot 3 works'. The build as delivered keeps LOT-1; the mutant gives None.
review_findings.fix: Add an ADDED-shape case to `a_title_designator_the_matched_lot_also_carries_agrees_5071935`: move the 'lot 06' designator from LOT-3's title into its TED-LOT_DESCRIPTION and assert that RES-3 still keeps LOT-3.

review_findings.title: The bucketed-path test's G4 chain (5020611) does not depend on G4
review_findings.evidence: `the_unit7_guards_are_identical_on_the_bucketed_path` says it checks one chain per guard, with (5020611, "G4") as the G4 chain. With G4 removed (mutant `g4off`), this test stays green, because G3 still moves 5020611's RES-1, RES-3 and RES-4 away from the unguarded fold. The G3 (8327340), G5 (4854639) and G6 (5001424) chains each fail when their own guard is removed. G4 on the bucket path is still covered indirectly, since every guard test folds through `r208_fold`.
review_findings.fix: Use 5051007 (refused by G4 alone, 19 blocks) as the bucketed test's G4 chain, or add it next to 5020611.

fixer:
All six findings were real. Each is fixed or pinned by a test, the decided rule is unchanged, and both focused runs pass with `GATE-EXIT=0`. Nothing was committed and `ops/check.sh` was not run. The only file I changed is `/home/user/tender-db/crates/ingest/src/project.rs`.

**Per finding:**

1. **Designator reader case handling (minor): real, fixed with Option A, matching the reference.**
   - I confirmed it in Python: `LOTS 3 ET 2` gives [3], `CZĘŚĆ NR 1 I 2` gives [1], `PAKIETY 1 DO 4` gives [1], and `Lot vi, VII` gives []. The Rust reader gave the case-insensitive answers.
   - Fix: `designator_next` now matches conjunctions and range words exactly, through a new `designator_exact`. `designator_number_at` accepts a Roman word only when it is upper-case MDCLXVI. The postfix scan reads the same as before, since a lower-case Roman normalises to nothing there.
